chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not make for people in their deeds any proof (hujjah) except through the knowledge of the Imam. For whoever dies without knowing his Imam, dies a death of ignorance (jahiliyyah).
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of dying without knowing the Imam according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the doctrine of *al-Hujjiyyah*, asserting that the Imam’s infallible authority is the necessary criterion for validating all acts of worship and belief. This establishes that recognition (*ma'rifah*) of the Imam is not merely a supplementary virtue but the foundational proof (*hujjah*) that distinguishes true faith from the *Jahiliyyah* (ignorance) of the pre-Islamic era.
